inputs.share_count_basis: Issued 3,175,762,284 less treasury 56,085,955 at 30-Sep-2026 (H1 FY2027 tanshin, post 4-for-1 split of 1-Jul-2026). The filing states there are no potentially dilutive common shares, so basic = fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is nil and the company is not a repurchaser (FY2026 buybacks JPY 13m), so no non-SBC issuance or retirement is modelled.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30-Sep-2026 balance sheet: short-term debt 281,904 + commercial paper 77,578 + current bonds 48,000 + bonds 112,000 + long-term debt 185,415 = 704,897; cash and cash equivalents 225,094 (CSV H1 FY2027). No lease liabilities: J-GAAP, operating leases expensed; the ASBJ lease standard is adopted only from the FY ending March 2028.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment line in the J-GAAP consolidated statements or notes (FY2026 annual, cash flow statement and equity note); EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year. SBC-zero market: SBC rows kept explicit at 0%, house and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: InterestAndDividendIncome FY2026 (interest 2.9bn + dividends 8.4bn) stripped from reported FCF under the matching-asset rule: the AFS securities that pay these dividends sit in the equity bridge at value, so their income must leave the flows. Forward EBITDA is built from J-GAAP operating profit, which already excludes interest, dividend and equity-method income.
inputs.fy0_note: Repo label FY2026 = fiscal year ended 31 March 2026 (the company calls it FY2025). Year 1 of the projection is FY2027 (ending 31 March 2027), the year guided in the 30-Oct-2026 H1 tanshin.
inputs.price_note: The H1 FY2027 results and the second guidance raise of the year were released on 30-Oct-2026 after the close, so this price predates them; the first post-release print is Monday 2-Nov-2026 and the upside figures should be re-read after it. Yahoo's 52-week high (3,712.5) is not split-adjusted; the post-split range is roughly 1,400-1,900.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-denominated flows discounted at a JPY-built rate: 10y JGB ~1.7% + 6.0% ERP x beta ~1.15 = ~8.6% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~2.0% (bonds 0.15-0.81%, JPY bank debt 1.5%, foreign-currency short-term debt 4.35%), ~1.5% after tax; D/(D+E) ~11% at the 30-Sep-2026 debt and the current market cap. Rounded to 8.0%, used in every scenario. Below the ~9% house reference for JPY keiretsu suppliers because this is a diversified, 55%-equity-ratio group with a top-two global position rather than a single-customer Tier-1. Cyclicality (auto build rates, copper, yen, tariffs, the AI-optical cycle) is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate, so no premium is stacked.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) by construction: operating leases are expensed inside J-GAAP operating profit (hence inside the EBITDA margin driver) and no lease liabilities sit in net debt. Nothing deducted twice; nothing omitted. Re-check when the ASBJ lease standard is adopted for the FY ending March 2028, which will move leases onto the balance sheet.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI deducted once in the bridge at book (JPY 89,633m at 30-Sep-2026). NCI fell from 240bn to 92bn in FY2026 when control of Sumitomo Densetsu was sold, and the H1 FY2027 NCI profit share was ~JPY 4bn (163.7bn net vs 159.4bn attributable), so ~JPY 9bn/yr against a 90bn deduction is consistent.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, 10-year horizon (routing table row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials'; owner-fcf.md and owner-fcf-adaptations.md both read). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. J-GAAP throughout, no IFRS break. CALIBRATION: FY2027 guidance OP 500bn x (1-27%) = 365bn + equity-method ~39bn + dividends/interest ~13bn - net interest ~20bn - NCI ~9bn = ~388bn vs guided attributable 370bn, i.e. the operating-profit-based build ties to the company's own net income within non-operating noise. BRIDGE: every stripped income stream has its asset in the bridge and vice versa -- dividend/interest income out, AFS securities in; equity-method profit out (never in operating profit), affiliates in at book. The JPY 344.9bn net defined-benefit asset is deliberately excluded (not realisable by shareholders). The 4-for-1 split is already in the CSV's per-share history; nothing re-adjusted here. SBC-zero market: band_position is null because house and street coincide.
inputs.mid_term_plan_note: Mid-term Management Plan 2028 (May 2026): FY ending Mar-2029 sales JPY 6tn, OP JPY 600bn (10.0% margin), pre-tax ROIC >15%. Set before the two FY2027 guidance raises; the sales target is already ~96% reached by the FY2027 guide, so the base case passes it in year 3 while reaching the 10% OP margin only in year 5 (two years later than the plan).

equity_bridge.item: Available-for-sale securities (cross-shareholdings) at fair value, net of deferred tax on the unrealized gain
equity_bridge.note: 31-Mar-2026 FY2026 annual note 5: fair value 374,159 (listed equities 367,953 with acquisition cost 19,178 and unrealized gain 348,937, plus 6,206 unlisted at cost) less 30.6% statutory tax on the unrealized gain (106,775) = 267,384; rolled to 30-Sep-2026 by the +61,206 after-tax increase in the AOCI unrealized-gains reserve (241,274 -> 302,480 in the H1 FY2027 balance sheet) = 328,590. Their ~JPY 8bn of dividends are stripped from the flows.

equity_bridge.item: Investments in unconsolidated subsidiaries and affiliates (equity method) at book
equity_bridge.note: 31-Mar-2026 balance sheet (latest audited split; the 30-Sep-2026 combined 'Investment securities' line of 819,967 is not disaggregated in the tanshin). Share of profit JPY 19.6bn in H1 FY2027 (~39bn annualised), i.e. book is ~8.7x earnings -- held at book, not marked up. This income never enters J-GAAP operating profit, so it is not in the flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case average revenue growth over years 1-5 (12.5/5/4/3.5/3). The equity 5-yr CAGR (11.0%) was rejected as the forward proxy because ~JPY 620bn of the JPY 2.74tn equity is AOCI (yen translation and unrealized securities gains) and the revenue CAGR is inflated by copper pass-through and yen depreciation; neither is repeatable growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs (46-49%) diverge >30pp from revenue (8-12%) and equity (11-13%): the FY2021 base was a COVID trough (EPS 18.06) and FY2026 EPS 118.45 includes the one-off gain on the sale of Sumitomo Densetsu (guided FY2027 EPS 118.60 is flat on a 20% OP increase for that reason). Treat the EPS CAGRs as cycle recovery, not trend.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on the repo's FY labels: FY2026 (y/e Mar-2026) vs FY2023 and FY2021. Owner FCF = reported FCF less interest and dividend income (SBC nil): FY2026 191,712, FY2023 74,419, FY2021 -2,076 -- the 5-yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined from a negative base and the 3-yr figure (37%) runs off a weak FY2023 (working-capital unwind year). Reported-FCF 3-yr CAGR 36.0% for reference. All growth on 3,119.7m post-split shares.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = the 30-Oct-2026 guidance (+12.5% to JPY 5,750bn; H1 was +16.5%, the guide implies H2 +9%). Y2-3 fade to 5%/4% as the copper and yen tailwinds stop compounding while AI-optical (Infocomm +46% in FY2026) and E&E grid demand carry mid-single digits; Y4-10 glide to 2% JPY nominal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 EBITDA margin 12.3% (OP 8.2% + D&A 4.1%); FY2027 guide OP 500bn on 5,750bn = 8.7% OP, ~12.6% EBITDA. Ramps to 14.0% (OP ~9.8%) by Y5 -- the mid-term plan's 10% OP margin, two years late. Automotive stays a ~6% margin business; the lift comes from Infocomm mix (23.7% margin), E&E and productivity.
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex 4.35% of sales in FY2026, 4.5% H1 FY2027 run-rate; held at 4.6% through the plan's investment phase (InP substrates 3.1x, HV harness plant in Spain, ~JPY 1tn 3-year investment envelope) then 4.3%. D&A 4.0% (FY2026 4.1%, H1 4.0%) drifting to 4.2% as capex runs above D&A.
base.tax_rationale: Statutory 30.6%; FY2025 effective 27.0%; FY2026 20.6% included a one-off non-taxable dividend (-4.0pp). Recurring tax credits (-2.5pp) and lower overseas rates (-3.1pp) justify 27% cash rate; cash taxes paid FY2026 64.4bn.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: receivables 961bn + inventories 1,220bn - payables 555bn = JPY 1.6tn (~30% of sales) at 30-Sep-2026, so growth consumes cash. H1 FY2027 inventories rose 200bn on +391bn YoY revenue. -20% of the revenue change (Y1 ~-128bn) is the base.
base.terminal_rationale: Cyclical industrial: 15x terminal cap (method range 12-15x for cyclicals); Gordon at 8%/2% would be 17x so the cap binds. 2.0% nominal JPY growth.

bull.rationale: A third beat-and-raise (Y1 +14%, i.e. H2 matches H1's +16%), AI data-centre optical demand sustained through FY2029 with InP capacity 3.1x and Infocomm becoming a 10%+ share of sales at 20%+ margins, grid/EV-harness growth in E&E, and auto volumes flat-to-up. EBITDA margin 15% (OP ~10.7%) exceeds the plan's 10% OP target. Higher capex funds the growth; WC drag lighter as inventory normalises.

bear.rationale: FY2027 lands short of guidance (+10%: tariffs, a weaker H2 for auto, the JPY 23bn Middle East headwind widening), then an auto downturn plus yen strength and copper reversal take FY2028 revenue down 3% with EBITDA margin back to 10.5% (OP ~6%, the FY2023-24 level) as the AI-optical cycle rolls over like prior fibre gluts. Margins recover only to 12% (OP ~7.8%, FY2025 level). 12x terminal cap, 1% terminal growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Sumitomo Electric delivers the twice-raised FY2027 guidance (sales JPY 5.75tn, OP JPY 500bn), then growth normalises to mid-single digits as copper pass-through and yen weakness stop inflating the top line. The axes that matter are (1) whether the generative-AI optical demand that took Infocommunications to a 23.7% margin on +46% sales persists long enough to become a durable mix shift, (2) whether the ~57%-of-sales Automotive harness business holds its ~6% margin through tariffs, EV-architecture simplification and labour inflation in assembly regions, and (3) whether E&E grid and EV-magnet-wire demand keeps compounding. Base assumes all three hold moderately: EBITDA margin reaches 14% (OP ~9.8%) by FY2031 -- the mid-term plan's 10% OP target two years late -- capex stays above D&A through the investment phase, working capital consumes 20% of each yen of growth, and the terminal value is capped at 15x FCF for a cyclical.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI data-centre fibre, optical devices and InP substrates compound for several more years, Infocomm doubles its share of group sales at 20%+ margins, E&E rides grid modernisation and 800V EV harnesses, and Automotive volumes stay flat-to-up with no tariff shock. Management beats the plan: 15% EBITDA margin (OP ~10.7%) by FY2031, growth 14%/8%/6% in the first three years. The ~JPY 1tn investment envelope is spent productively, and the cross-shareholding sales continue to recycle capital at book-plus.
scenario_narratives.bear: The three things that could go wrong go wrong together: an auto-production downturn or US auto-parts tariffs hit the thin-margin harness business (as in FY2022-23 when Automotive earned JPY 12bn on JPY 1.75tn of sales), yen appreciation and a copper reversal deflate the top line, and hyperscaler optical capex normalises after the 2025-26 surge. FY2028 revenue falls 3%, EBITDA margin drops to 10.5% and only recovers to 12%. The terminal value is capped at 12x; the equity bridge (securities, affiliates) still provides a floor. No solvency question at a 55% equity ratio.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 shifted to 25/50/25. Bear up from 15% because 57% of sales is a ~6% margin auto-harness business exposed to build rates, tariffs, copper and the yen at once, and the AI-optical surge that drove the FY2026 margin step-up has a cyclical history (fibre gluts). Bull down from 35% because it needs auto to stay flat AND AI optical to persist AND margins to exceed the mid-term plan, three independent conditions. Balance sheet (55% equity ratio, net debt 0.7x EBITDA) removes any going-concern weight.

entry_price.note: House 15% hurdle applied to JPY flows; against a ~1.7% JGB it is a demanding bar, which is why the entry prices sit well below intrinsic value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a diversified cyclical on consolidated owner FCF built from J-GAAP operating profit, with every non-operating income stream stripped and its asset added back once in the bridge (AFS cross-shareholdings after tax, equity-method affiliates at book, NCI deducted). Cyclicality is priced in three explicit flow paths and a 25% bear weight, not in the discount rate; the terminal value is capped at a cyclical's multiple so that the Y10 margin, not a growth assumption, carries the valuation. House and street coincide because SBC is nil.
key_risks_to_valuation: Automotive (57% of sales) is a ~6% margin business: a global auto downturn or US auto-parts tariffs can take group OP down 30-40% quickly (FY2022 Automotive OP JPY 12bn vs JPY 180bn in FY2026)
Copper price and JPY: both inflated FY2026-27 revenue; a reversal deflates the top line and lags pass-through compress margins
AI-optical cycle: Infocomm's margin went from -5.6% (FY2024) to 23.7% (FY2026) on hyperscaler demand; prior fibre cycles ended in gluts
Equity bridge is ~JPY 185/share of the value: cross-shareholding fair values move with the Nikkei and realisation is taxed; affiliates held at book
Price predates the 30-Oct-2026 H1 release and guidance raise; upside figures must be re-read after the first post-release close
Mid-term plan's ~JPY 1tn investment could run above the 4.6% capex assumption, or be spent on M&A outside the model
